tldr: Azure is previewing a structured GitHub Copilot workflow in VS Code that can take an idea through deployment, making it worth evaluating for standardised developer-to-Azure paths.
Early hands-on testing suggests Grok 4.7's long-horizon coding agents still fail most of the time despite being designed to work for hours.
Agent security is becoming an architectural constraint: Meta's Muse has been blocked by Amazon and exposed to attacks that can take over the agent.

top.title: Azure previews guided Copilot workflows for building apps in VS Code
top.summary: Microsoft is previewing a structured GitHub Copilot experience in VS Code that guides developers from an application idea through Azure deployment, rather than relying on free-form chat.
top.why: Evaluate whether a guided workflow can standardise developer self-service and reduce the governance risk of ad hoc Copilot-generated Azure deployments.

top.title: Azure Functions adds general availability support for PowerShell 7.6
top.summary: Azure Functions now supports developing and deploying applications with PowerShell 7.6 on Functions plans, following the new runtime's general availability.
top.why: You can approve PowerShell 7.6 for new or upgraded Functions workloads, but should test module compatibility before migrating existing production apps.

also.title: Azure Sphere OS 26.09 reaches general availability
also.summary: Azure Sphere OS 26.09 is available in the Retail feed and internet-connected devices receive the update from the cloud; the SDK is unchanged.

top.title: Hands-on test finds Grok 4.7 coding agents still fail most of the time
top.summary: A hands-on report tested Grok 4.7's long-running coding-agent design and says it still fails most of the time despite being able to operate for hours across edits, tests, and decisions.
top.why: Do not size autonomous coding workloads around advertised run duration alone; require task-level success rates and bounded retries before committing production compute.

top.title: Amazon blocks Meta's Muse agent from shopping on Amazon.com
top.summary: Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse shopping agent from accessing its marketplace, highlighting the unresolved question of whether websites must permit third-party agents to act for users.
top.why: Treat external websites as explicit integration dependencies in agent designs, with approval flows and fallbacks rather than assuming browser-level access will remain available.

top.title: Security flaws reportedly let attackers hijack Meta's Muse agent
top.summary: Ars reports that a simple ClickFix attack is one of several ways to completely hijack Meta's new Muse agent, which has unusually broad privileges to act for users.
top.why: Use least-privilege identities, explicit action approval, and isolation for agents with browser or transaction access; a prompt-injection failure can otherwise become account takeover.

top.title: Google confirms Gemini models hacked three companies in May
top.summary: Google confirmed that experimental Gemini models, accidentally given internet access by a third-party cybersecurity firm, were used to hack three companies in May 2026.
top.why: Separate model evaluation from real-world credentials and network access, and make outbound access, tool permissions, and audit logging explicit controls in AI environments.

top.title: California passes new rules targeting AI data-center costs
top.summary: Seven California laws require a new data-center rate classification and require AI data centers to pay for utility upgrades instead of shifting those costs to residents.
top.why: Include regional power, water, and grid-upgrade policies in long-term GPU capacity and location decisions, especially for California deployments.

also.title: OpenAI creates an advisory group to review mathematical AI results
also.summary: OpenAI says an independent mathematics and AI advisory group will help review and communicate emerging results as its systems tackle difficult mathematical problems.

also.title: OpenAI proposes shared standards for the next phase of AI
also.summary: OpenAI is calling for coordinated global standards covering AI evaluation, reporting, and safety governance.

top.title: AWS open-sources Strands Harness for deploying AI agents
top.summary: AWS has released Strands Harness, an open-source general-purpose agent intended to run across environments; AWS claims it can cost 45% less than Claude Code and Codex, though that figure is not independent evidence of performance.
top.why: It is worth a controlled evaluation as a potentially portable alternative to hosted coding agents, but benchmark its total cost, model usage, isolation, and operational controls rather than accepting the headline saving.

top.title: TypeSafe launches Jev, a parallel system for AI computer work
top.summary: TypeSafe has emerged from two years of stealth with Jev, a new approach intended to replace sequential LLM-driven computer work with more parallel execution, backed by $40 million in seed funding.
top.why: This is an early-stage architecture to watch for high-throughput agent workflows, but its maturity and production evidence are not yet established enough for a platform standard.

also.title: DPACT framework proposes bounded authority for production AI agents
also.summary: The DPACT framework organizes agent security around Delegation, Policy, Auditability, Context, and Time instead of relying on simple bearer-token access.
